title: Cap. VIII: Ex vs.18 — through is not on account of
pass_a_gloss: Next head: from verse 18 Garissoles gathers by the same pattern used above. Major: if through someone's offense condemnation came on all humans, then on account of that someone's offense a penalty is laid on everyone. Minor: through the one Adam's offense condemnation did come on everyone. Conclusion: therefore on account of the one Adam's offense a penalty is laid on all his descendants. Placeus's first cut: the major can be refused. Being through someone is not the same as being on account of someone. Illustrations: writing happens through a pen, not on account of the pen; condemnation happens through a judge, not on account of the judge.
pass_b_english: V. From verse 18 he gathers by a similar reason as above. The one through whose offense condemnation came upon all human beings — on account of that one's offense a penalty is inflicted on all. But through one Adam's offense condemnation came upon all. Therefore on account of one Adam's offense a penalty is inflicted on all his posterity (Romans 5:18). First, the major premise can be denied. For it is one thing for something to be through someone, another for it to be on account of someone: I write with a pen, yet not on account of the pen; condemnation is through a judge, yet not on account of the judge.
source_text: V. Ex verf. 18. simili ratione ac supra colligit. Per cuius delictum condemnatio in omnes homines venit, propter illius delictum poena irrogatur omnibus: Atqui per unius Adae delictum condemnatio venit in omnes. Ergo propter unius Adae delictum, poena irrogatur omnibus ejus posteris. Primum negari potest major propositio. aliud enim est per aliquem esse aliquid, aliud propter aliquem; per calamum scribo, non tamen propter calamum; per judicem est condemnatio, non tamen propter judicem.
